data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** de72c6dd68c5558f312d42e9793ea9e1a5979503

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

When \`merge-to-main.sh\` creates the PR for a sprint session that's been working on a specific epic, the PR title should reference the epic that the session was implementing — e.g., \`fix(a34c): in-process ticket_list --has-tag + cascade fixes for closure\` or \`[a34c-b345-1e63-4ae3] Calibration program observability\`.

Per \`_derive_pr_title\` in \`plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh\` lines 378–435, the priority order is documented as:
1. Latest non-merge commit subject reachable from main..HEAD
2. If subject already starts with \`[<id>]\`, return as-is
3. Otherwise extract DSO-Story/DSO-Task trailer or branch-local \`[<id>]\` prefix
4. Fallback to \`[<branch>] <merge-subject>\`

The session's actual work commits all carry \`fix(a34c):\`/\`feat(a34c):\` subjects and reference the epic in description bodies, so the latest non-merge commit on a sprint session branch (before merge-to-main.sh runs) should map cleanly to the epic.

#### Actual Behavior

PR #266 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/266) was created with title:

\`\`\`
[0e61-caa3-3cb1-4451] chore: bump version to v1.17.11
\`\`\`

The session's actual work was on epic \`a34c-b345-1e63-4ae3\` (Calibration program observability) — 5+ commits with \`fix(a34c):\`/\`feat(a34c):\` prefixes. The PR title references neither the epic ID nor the epic name. The bracketed prefix \`[0e61-caa3-3cb1-4451]\` came from a DSO-Story trailer on the version-bump commit (which attributes to an unrelated task from earlier in the session), and the body \`chore: bump version to v1.17.11\` is the version-bump commit subject.

Root cause sketch:
\`merge-to-main-pr.sh\` creates its own version-bump commit (e.g. \`chore: bump version to v1.17.11\`) immediately before calling \`gh pr create\`. \`_derive_pr_title\` then reads \`git log --no-merges -1 --pretty=%s main..HEAD\` which returns the version-bump subject because it's the latest non-merge commit. The trailer extraction in step 3a finds a DSO-Story trailer on the version-bump commit and prepends it, producing a title that reflects neither the session's primary work nor the epic.

### 3. Action History

* User invoked \`/dso:sprint a34c-b345-1e63-4ae3\` to execute the Calibration program observability epic
* Session ran multiple stories and committed 5+ \`fix(a34c)\` / \`feat(a34c)\` commits
* User invoked \`.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh\` to merge work to main
* merge-to-main-pr.sh created a version-bump commit then ran \`gh pr create\`
* The PR title became \`[0e61-caa3-3cb1-4451] chore: bump version to v1.17.11\`

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The PR title-derivation logic was hardened in PR #171 retro-review (commit message references that) to avoid scanning main history. But the in-script version-bump commit on the source branch is itself the artifact that pollutes the latest-commit lookup. The version-bump commit must be excluded from title derivation, OR the title must be derived from the session ticket / epic ID stored elsewhere.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affected skill: \`/dso:sprint\` (Phase F merge-to-main invocation)
* Affected script: \`plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh\` (\`_derive_pr_title\`)
* Related: SC of any epic relying on PR titles for traceability

### 6. Logs

Diagnostic:

\`\`\`
\$ git rev-parse HEAD
de72c6dd68c5558f312d42e9793ea9e1a5979503

\$ git log --no-merges -1 --pretty=%s main..HEAD
fix(a34c): cut CI runtime of detected_by integration + audit tests

\$ gh pr view 266 --json title
{"title":"[0e61-caa3-3cb1-4451] chore: bump version to v1.17.11"}
\`\`\`

The current latest non-merge commit DOES reference a34c, but at PR creation time the version-bump commit was latest. The bug reproduces whenever merge-to-main-pr.sh creates a version-bump commit before calling \`gh pr create\`.

#### Suggested fix (informational, not prescriptive)

Options:
1. Exclude version-bump commits from title derivation (\`git log --no-merges -1 --pretty=%s --grep -v "^chore: bump version" main..HEAD\`)
2. Use the session ticket ID from \`.sprint-active\` marker or epic ID stored in tracker
3. Reorder so PR is created BEFORE the version bump (version bump becomes a follow-up commit on the PR branch)
4. Pass an explicit \`--title-source-commit <sha>\` argument to \`merge-to-main-pr.sh\` that the caller supplies (e.g., from sprint Phase F handoff)
data.title: [merge-to-main-pr]: sprint-session PR creation -> title derived from version-bump commit instead of epic ID
